name: Additional connector pin
summary: A further pin of a connector already tagged elsewhere, drawn without repeating the connector body or tag.
description: On schematics a connector often has pins scattered across several circuits and sheets. The first pin carries the connector tag and body, and each additional pin is drawn with a lighter child symbol that refers back to it. This avoids drawing the same connector several times with conflicting tags.

Readers should treat every child pin as part of the parent connector, so separating the connector disconnects all of them. The child symbol does not repeat the connector type or rating, which must be read from the parent. Pin numbers on child symbols must still be unique within the connector.
readingNotes: Find the parent connector tag for each child pin.
Remember all child pins separate when the connector is unplugged.
drawingChecklist: Cross-reference child pins to the parent.
State connector data only on the parent.
distinction: An additional connector pin is a child of a tagged connector; a standalone plug and socket pair is a connector in its own right.
